title: React Module 08 Core Check
description: Check your understanding of custom Hooks, extraction, naming, inputs, return values, reuse of stateful logic, common hooks, and testing awareness.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: A reusable function that starts with `use` and can call other Hooks

questions.explanation: Custom Hooks extract reusable stateful logic into functions named with the `use` prefix.

questions.prompt: Custom Hook names should start with `use`.
questions.explanation: The `use` prefix communicates Hook behavior and lets lint tooling enforce Hook rules.

questions.prompt: What should usually stay outside a custom Hook?

options.text: Calls to built-in Hooks needed by the logic

questions.explanation: Custom Hooks should usually return data and behavior, while components render the UI.

questions.prompt: When is extracting a custom Hook useful? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The same stateful logic is repeated in multiple components
A component is hard to read because logic and UI are tangled
You want to share behavior without sharing markup
You have one clear line of code used once

questions.explanation: Hooks are useful for repeated or complex stateful behavior, not for needless abstraction.

questions.prompt: What should a custom Hook return?

options.text: Whatever API makes the consuming component clear, such as values and functions

questions.explanation: Custom Hooks can return arrays or objects; the API should make usage clear and stable.

questions.prompt: Which is a common custom Hook example?
questions.explanation: `useToggle` is a typical custom Hook that manages boolean state and toggle behavior.

questions.prompt: Which concerns belong in a custom Hook that uses effects? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Calling Hooks conditionally after an early return
Clear inputs for values the hook depends on

questions.explanation: Custom Hooks follow the same Hook rules as components and should manage dependencies and cleanup carefully.

questions.prompt: Each component call to a custom Hook gets its own independent Hook state.
questions.explanation: A custom Hook shares logic, not one shared state instance across all callers.
